description: Scandium is a silvery-white metallic element with symbol Sc and atomic number 21, found in the d-block of the periodic table and usually classified as a rare-earth element together with yttrium and the lanthanides. It is a soft metal that develops a slightly yellowish or pinkish cast when oxidized by air, and it is susceptible to weathering and dissolves slowly in most dilute acids. In nature, scandium is found exclusively as the stable isotope 45Sc.
uses: The main application of scandium is in aluminium-scandium alloys for aerospace industry components, which limit grain growth in welded aluminium and strengthen the material through Al3Sc precipitate formation. Scandium is also used in metal-halide lamps as a high-intensity discharge light source, with approximately 20 kg used annually in the United States for this purpose. Additionally, scandium-stabilized zirconia is used as a high-efficiency electrolyte in solid oxide fuel cells, and scandium is employed as a Lewis acid catalyst in organic chemistry.
characteristics: Scandium is a soft metal with intermediate chemical properties between aluminium and yttrium, and it exhibits a diagonal relationship with magnesium similar to the relationship between beryllium and aluminium. The element has low availability as it occurs sparsely in trace amounts in many minerals and is distributed unevenly in Earth's crust at an abundance of 18-25 ppm. Scandium compounds are almost completely dominated by the trivalent ion Sc3+, and while compounds with other oxidation states are rare, they have been well characterized.
